scope: Complete current official finite Pendle Router deployment map intersected with supported chains 1,10,56,137,143,8453,42161; exact existing protocol label pendle-v3 only. Same-address selector-dispatch/facet binding and fixed typed financial capability expansion, including existing Ethereum router. No arbitrary SY/market/factory enumeration, new chains, execution languages, grants or protocol versions.
sourceReviewBoundary: Target-bound source/ABI and block-pinned dispatch observations are inventory evidence, not future runtime persistence, funding, balances, liquidity, complete-workflow, successful execution or financial-safety attestation.

currentOfficialDocumentation.evidence: Current developer deployments page explicitly links chain-specific core JSON, including all six admitted supported-chain routers. Polygon is not listed. Page instructs use of implementation ABIs from explorer or code.

officialMaps.lifecycleReview: All six targeted Router deployments are explicitly in current official Supported Chains deployment documentation and outside deprecated manifest sections. No deprecated/sunset-only router is admitted. Unsupported-chain manifests are preserved only to make finite-map exclusion auditable; they add no capabilities.
officialMaps.mapFreshnessWarning: Official manifests name historical facet roles, but current block-pinned dispatch differs on five chains. Manifest role correspondence is not installed selector proof. Actual returned facet addresses and their own target-bound sources/ABIs, not copied Ethereum ABI, control admission. Optimism still resolves documented facets.

evidenceEncoding.sourcePool: SHA-256 keyed exact UTF-8 source text, manifest JSON, explorer HTML, bytecode strings and other raw receipts. Solidity contents are raw source text, never Python/tool-response repr. Contract receipts map every compilation source path to its pooled content hash.
evidenceEncoding.abiPool: Full untrimmed deployed ABI arrays, including events/errors/constructors/receive/fallback where present, keyed by SHA-256 of recursively key-sorted compact UTF-8 JSON with array order retained. Each function inventory binds its own chain-specific facet receipt.
evidenceEncoding.reportedGrades: Sourcify exact_match and match are retained literally, with underlying creationMatch/runtimeMatch, verifier timestamps, compilation/deployment metadata and bytecode receipts. MonadScan Contract Source Code Verified (Exact Match) remains an explorer grade, not invented Sourcify verification.
evidenceEncoding.dispatchCompleteness: Finite inventory is the complete ABI-function union of documented and observed installed facets of this one router deployment family. All 56 signatures have selectorToFacet eth_call receipts on each reviewed chain. This does not claim enumeration of unknown mapping keys unrelated to that finite official map. Constructors, fallback, receive, events and errors are evidence only, never capabilities.

deployments.labelContinuity: Exact existing pendle-v3 label preserved. Source contract name PendleRouterV4 describes the existing address dispatcher; no new protocol label/version is introduced.
deployments.dispatchArchitecture: Verified PendleRouterV4 fallback looks up RouterStorage.selectorToFacet[msg.sig] and delegates to that address. ActionStorageV4.selectorToFacet(bytes4) reads that same mapping; every finite candidate selector has its own block-pinned eth_call receipt below. functionInventory.reason: Adds LP from caller SY and PT using fixed typed amounts and minimum LP; market mint is fixed, no executor payload.
TokenInput includes caller-selected pendleSwap/swapData external router, opaque calldata and scaling flag; dual-token LP method cannot be admitted as a fixed SY/PT method.
LimitOrderData contains caller limitRouter, signed order fills, optData and callback payload; no existing Pendle nested-execution language authorizes this surface.

Ordinary caller-PT single-sided LP mint with onchain approximation and minimum LP; no caller limit orders, callback bytes or swap executor. Source marks Simple internal-use/interface-unstable, but implementation is externally callable without an internal-only guard.
LimitOrderData allows signed order execution and caller callback/optData in addition to approximation; not equivalent to the payload-free Simple method.
Splits caller SY into PY and LP while retaining YT for receiver; fixed minimum LP/YT parameters and no opaque route data.

Ordinary caller-SY single-sided LP mint with onchain approximation and minimum LP; no caller limit orders or opaque routes. Source Simple internal-use/interface-instability notice is retained as a warning, not an invented authorization condition.
Combines arbitrary TokenInput.swapData execution with LimitOrderData order/callback payloads; fixed outer ABI does not authorize nested execution.
TokenInput can select external swap executor and opaque swapData; keep-YT economics do not remove executor authority.
Simple variant still accepts TokenInput external executor and opaque swapData; its name does not make it a fixed typed SY method.
Refreshes caller market reward/voting boost through fixed zero-amount market transferFrom calls. Consumes pre-existing token authority only and grants none; no arbitrary call bytes.
Read-only transient SY redeemer context getter; not a transaction capability.
Arbitrary selfCall1/selfCall2 delegatecall bytes and caller reflector reflectCall admit nested opaque execution.
Administrative pending-owner acceptance changes router ownership; not financial user action.
Combines LP removal and matured PT redemption into receiver SY with minimum SY; fixed market/YT methods, no route bytes.
Matured exit TokenOutput still accepts caller-selected swap executor and opaque swapData; direct SY exit is admitted instead.
Pre-expiry exit can invoke caller LimitOrderData signed fills and callback bytes; no fixed-payload subset restriction is invented.
Both TokenOutput external swap and LimitOrderData order/callback languages are present.
Callback handler accepts opaque callback data and is for protocol-initiated limit-router settlement, not an independent user financial action.
Transfers caller SY and mints matched PT/YT to receiver with typed minimum PY; no swap executor.
TokenInput external aggregator and opaque swapData are unadmitted; direct mintPyFromSy has no such payload.
TokenInput permits caller-selected swap router/executor and opaque data; separate SY deposit root is intentionally unchanged.
Arbitrary nested self-delegatecall bytes plus allowFailure semantics have no current Pendle execution-scope validator.
Read-only current router owner getter; transaction capability and read API are not added.
Read-only pending-router-owner getter; no transaction capability.
Claims SY/YT/market rewards and YT interest for explicit user through three fixed method loops; address arrays are typed targets, not executable calldata.
V2 rewards can route claimed assets through caller pendleSwap and SwapDataExtra opaque swap payloads; no empty-swaps-only execution language is added.
Redeems caller PY through its YT into SY with typed minimum; consumes existing token authority without granting new authority.
TokenOutput includes external swap executor/opaque calldata; direct PY-to-SY redemption is admitted instead.
TokenOutput allows generic external swaps and arbitrary swap data; not equivalent to payload-free SY redeem.
Burns caller LP to explicit receiver SY/PT with independent typed minimums; fixed market burn path.
TokenOutput allows caller-selected external swap executor and opaque swap calldata while redeeming SY; not the admitted direct SY/PT output.
LimitOrderData accepts external limit router/order fills and caller callback bytes; excluded even though a zero-limit-data subset could avoid them.

Burns caller LP and swaps SY remainder into PT under minimum PT; fixed market calls with protocol-generated or empty callback data, no caller execution payload. Simple interface-instability notice retained.
LimitOrderData can dispatch signed fills/opaque callback data; no new constrained-subset language is introduced.
Both TokenOutput swap executor/calldata and LimitOrderData callback/order execution are unconstrained by current capability model.
Emits RequestBurnQuota with optional opaque event data only; does not itself perform a supported deposit/redeem/swap or grant quota, so no financial action capability.
Read-only dispatch getter used only as inventory evidence; no read API/capability is added.
Owner-only mutable selector-to-facet dispatch administration can replace execution implementations; excluded.
Caller target.delegatecall(data) is arbitrary execution even though the function deliberately reverts with simulation results; not a financial capability.
Market callback handler decodes action bytes; no direct callback capability or new caller-provided callback language.
LimitOrderData carries caller-selected limit router and callback/optData order-execution language; direct SY output alone is insufficient.
TokenOutput external swap data and LimitOrderData signed-order/callback paths are unadmitted nested execution.
Caller LimitOrderData can execute orders/callback bytes; ordinary fixed typed alternative is swapExactSyForPtSimple.
Exact caller-SY swap to receiver PT with typed minimum PT and onchain approximation; no caller swap data or limit-order callback. Simple interface-instability notice retained.
Caller LimitOrderData accepts order/callback execution; fixed typed alternative is swapExactSyForYtSimple.

Exact caller-SY swap to receiver YT with typed minimum YT; callback is generated internally from action enum/receiver/YT, not supplied as an opaque execution language. Simple interface-instability notice retained.
TokenInput opaque external swap and LimitOrderData order/callback paths require a new execution language.
TokenInput can select external aggregator and opaque calldata before PT swap; excluded despite Simple suffix.
Caller TokenInput swap executor/opaque data and LimitOrderData order callbacks remain unsupported.
TokenInput permits opaque external swap execution before YT swap; not the payload-free exact-SY Simple method.
LimitOrderData signed-order fills and callback/optData are an unadmitted execution language despite direct SY output.
TokenOutput opaque external swap plus LimitOrderData callbacks/orders remain excluded.
TokenInput includes external swap executor and opaque calldata; fixed token/SY addresses do not constrain nested execution.
Caller pendleSwap with SwapDataExtra arrays dispatches opaque swap calldata; no new aggregator execution language.
Router ownership transfer/renunciation administration is excluded.

    IPActionStorageEvents

pragma solidity ^0.8.0;

import {ExitPreExpReturnParams, ExitPostExpReturnParams} from "./IPAllActionTypeV3.sol";

interface IPActionAddRemoveLiqV3Events {
    event AddLiquidityDualSyAndPt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netSyUsed,
        uint256 netPtUsed,
        uint256 netLpOut
    );

    event AddLiquidityDualTokenAndPt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed tokenIn,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netTokenUsed,
        uint256 netPtUsed,
        uint256 netLpOut,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event AddLiquiditySinglePt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netPtIn,
        uint256 netLpOut
    );

    event AddLiquiditySingleSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netSyIn,
        uint256 netLpOut
    );

    event AddLiquiditySingleToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netTokenIn,
        uint256 netLpOut,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event AddLiquiditySingleSyKeepYt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netSyIn,
        uint256 netSyMintPy,
        uint256 netLpOut,
        uint256 netYtOut
    );

    event AddLiquiditySingleTokenKeepYt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netTokenIn,
        uint256 netLpOut,
        uint256 netYtOut,
        uint256 netSyMintPy,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event RemoveLiquidityDualSyAndPt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netLpToRemove,
        uint256 netPtOut,
        uint256 netSyOut
    );

    event RemoveLiquidityDualTokenAndPt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed tokenOut,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netLpToRemove,
        uint256 netPtOut,
        uint256 netTokenOut,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event RemoveLiquiditySinglePt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netLpToRemove,
        uint256 netPtOut
    );

    event RemoveLiquiditySingleSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netLpToRemove,
        uint256 netSyOut
    );

    event RemoveLiquiditySingleToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netLpToRemove,
        uint256 netTokenOut,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );
}

interface IPActionSwapPTV3Events {
    event SwapPtAndSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        int256 netPtToAccount,
        int256 netSyToAccount
    );

    event SwapPtAndToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        int256 netPtToAccount,
        int256 netTokenToAccount,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );
}

interface IPActionSwapYTV3Events {
    event SwapYtAndSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        int256 netYtToAccount,
        int256 netSyToAccount
    );

    event SwapYtAndToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        int256 netYtToAccount,
        int256 netTokenToAccount,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event SwapPtAndYt(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        int256 netPtToAccount,
        int256 netYtToAccount
    );
}

interface IPActionMiscV3Events {
    event MintSyFromToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed tokenIn,
        address indexed SY,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netTokenIn,
        uint256 netSyOut
    );

    event RedeemSyToToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed tokenOut,
        address indexed SY,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netSyIn,
        uint256 netTokenOut
    );

    event MintPyFromSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed receiver,
        address indexed YT,
        uint256 netSyIn,
        uint256 netPyOut
    );

    event RedeemPyToSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed receiver,
        address indexed YT,
        uint256 netPyIn,
        uint256 netSyOut
    );

    event MintPyFromToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed tokenIn,
        address indexed YT,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netTokenIn,
        uint256 netPyOut,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event RedeemPyToToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed tokenOut,
        address indexed YT,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netPyIn,
        uint256 netTokenOut,
        uint256 netSyInterm
    );

    event ExitPreExpToToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netLpIn,
        uint256 totalTokenOut,
        ExitPreExpReturnParams params
    );

    event ExitPreExpToSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netLpIn,
        ExitPreExpReturnParams params
    );

    event ExitPostExpToToken(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed token,
        address receiver,
        uint256 netLpIn,
        uint256 totalTokenOut,
        ExitPostExpReturnParams params
    );

    event ExitPostExpToSy(
        address indexed caller,
        address indexed market,
        address indexed receiver,
        uint256 netLpIn,
        ExitPostExpReturnParams params
    );
}

interface IPActionStorageEvents {
    event OwnershipTransferred(address indexed previousOwner, address indexed newOwner);

    event SelectorToFacetSet(bytes4 indexed selector, address indexed facet);
}

interface IPAllEventsV3 is
    IPActionAddRemoveLiqV3Events,
    IPActionSwapPTV3Events,
    IPActionSwapYTV3Events,
    IPActionMiscV3Events,
    IPActionStorageEvents
{}

 # this file every version of this package was published by hand from a personal
 # npm login. `prepack` runs `yarn compile`, so a publish compiles the contracts.
 #
+# ── Why /snapshot-release does not publish in its own run ─────────────────────
+# Since 2026-09-19 npm refuses the OIDC exchange for a token whose event_name
+# is issue_comment: HTTP 404 "OIDC token exchange error - package not found".
+# The same exchange with the same repository, workflow and environment returns
+# 201 on workflow_dispatch, on develop and on a feature branch (runs 35440283948,
+# 35440433396, 35439930999). npm does not document this. So the comment run only
+# authorises and pins the SHA, then dispatches this file on the default branch.
+# The publish always runs as workflow_dispatch.
+#
 # ── Adding a trigger ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 # Any new publish path must be a job here. A new workflow file that publishes
 # will fail the OIDC exchange, because the record names this filename.
@@ -35,6 +44,17 @@ on:
     branches:
       - main
   workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      # Set by the authorize job below. Empty on a manual dispatch.
+      sha:
+        description: Exact commit to snapshot (default is the dispatched ref)
+        required: false
+      branch_name:
+        description: Branch name for the snapshot suffix (default is the dispatched ref)
+        required: false
+      pr:
+        description: Pull request to comment the result on
+        required: false
   issue_comment:
     types: [created]
 
@@ -61,9 +81,7 @@ jobs:
       # the authorize job, so the snapshot job never runs and `/snapshot-release`
       # does nothing.
       pull-requests: write
-    outputs:
-      sha: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.sha }}
-      branch_name: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.branch_name }}
+      actions: write # dispatches the snapshot run
     steps:
       # author_association is NOT sufficient: COLLABORATOR includes read-only
       # collaborators, who can comment but must not be able to publish.
@@ -109,6 +127,21 @@ jobs:
               content: '+1',

Deployments

info

While interacting with contracts, please use the ABI of implementation contracts from a block explorer or generate the ABI from the smart contract code in GitHub.

Core Contracts​

Pendle's core contract addresses are organized by chain ID. You can find the latest contract addresses in the deployment files within the Pendle contract repository.

Each chain's deployment file follows the naming pattern: /deployments/{chainId}-core.json

SY / Market / PT / YT Addresses​

To find the relevant addresses and details of a specific market:

  1. Go to the Pendle markets page
  2. Select the desired chain and click into an asset
  3. Click into the button as shown in the image below to view all contract addresses
